## Summary

The repo already had OSV infrastructure for the *resolver* surface; the task was to wire OSV screening into the *registry* surface and refactor the tarball-name API.

### `package_name.rs`
- Removed `validate_tarball_name`. `parse_tarball_name` (returning `(canonical_filename, version)`) is now the primary validator; moved the "two accepted forms" contract documentation onto it and noted the OSV/canonicalization use. Kept `canonicalize_tarball_name` (a thin wrapper still used by the delete handler).

### `resolver/osv.rs`
- Added `is_vulnerable(&self, package, version) -> bool` (delegates to `vulnerability_ids`, so it inherits case-insensitive lookup and semver-range matching).
- Added `filter_packument(&self, package, &mut Value)`: removes a `versions` key when it isn't valid semver, when its `version` field disagrees with the key (identity mismatch), or when it's OSV-vulnerable — then drops those keys from `time` and drops any `dist-tags` entry pointing at a removed version.

- `load_active_osv_index` now loads the index when **registry or resolver** is enabled (previously resolver-only), so the registry can consult it.

- Packument (`packument_response`), version-manifest, and dist-tags read paths now apply `filter_packument` when OSV is enabled — deterministically, so cached and freshly-proxied responses filter identically, removed versions 404 on the manifest endpoint, and dist-tags drop tags targeting removed versions.
